name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing frequent patch updates across multiple supported major versions simultaneously. The latest release is v0.63.15 (open source) / v1.63.15 (enterprise), released on August 26, 2025 (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases/tag/v0.63.15). Multiple version branches (v59–v63) are maintained in parallel, each receiving concurrent patch releases, indicating a mature long-term support strategy. Detailed changelogs per release are linked from each release page on GitHub.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license.
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple patch releases across 5 major version branches were published on August 26, 2025.
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase offers a managed cloud (Metabase Cloud) at metabase.com.
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition.
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Athena, MongoDB, SQLite, Presto, Druid, Oracle, Vertica, SparkSQL, and more (varies by edition).

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Looker
alternatives.review: Offers a more robust governed data modeling layer via LookML compared to Metabase, but is significantly more expensive and not open source.

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Provides more advanced and polished data visualization capabilities than Metabase, but comes at a high cost and is a closed-source proprietary solution.
